t1.title: Kill mid-agent-loop; the restarted process (same replica, NEW executor ID) takes over
notes: A restart is a new process, so it is a new executor; Railway replica/deployment IDs are recorded as metadata only.
Takeover is by the heartbeat sweep (DEAD_AFTER_MS), not DBOS launch recovery. Completed model calls (turns 0,1) replayed from checkpoints.

t1b.title: Kill mid-agent-loop, NEW container (different executor ID) takes over
notes: DBOS alone would NOT recover this: launch recovery only reclaims PENDING rows for its own executor ID.
Adapter = ops.executors heartbeat + atomic reap + public DBOS.resumeWorkflows() (same workflow ID, checkpoints kept).
Recovery latency ≈ DEAD_AFTER_MS (5s in suite) + sweep interval.

t2.title: Kill executor after external call, before local checkpoint

metrics.requestAttemptsVsUniqueEffects: 3 attempts → 2 committed effects (1 deduplicated by provider)

notes: Executor workflow IDs equal the action idempotency keys; a second enqueue under the same ID returned the existing workflow.
The post-call/pre-checkpoint window is real: the provider saw the same key twice. Exactly-once effect came from the provider-side Idempotency-Key, as rule 3 says.

t3.title: Rolling deploy: old+new overlap with schedules running, then old disappears (SIGKILL)
notes: Two live schedulers never produced two runs for one occurrence (ID = sched-<name>-<scheduled ISO>).
During overlap the new container never claimed the old one's PENDING work (unique executor IDs).
Turns re-run more than once are only the calls in flight when the old container was killed; completed ones replayed from checkpoints.

t3b.title: Rolling deploy: old gets SIGTERM and drains in-flight work before exiting
notes: DBOS.shutdown({workflowCompletionTimeoutMS}) finished the in-flight run on the old container; nothing re-ran.

t4a.title: Deploy a step-inserting code change while work is mid-flight (patching mode + DBOS.patch)
notes: Old execution replayed its original step sequence on new code; new executions took the patched branch. Nothing stranded.

t4b.title: Same change WITHOUT DBOS.patch (the mistake rule 4 forbids)

metrics.settleMs: timed out after 25000ms waiting for both settle

notes: Expected-negative control: DBOS detects the step-sequence mismatch on replay and refuses to continue, instead of silently doing the wrong thing.
Classification is PASS if the unpatched change is caught and surfaced in health; it confirms the discipline is enforced, not optional.

t4c.title: Same deploy in build-version mode (DBOS__APPVERSION = build ID)

attentionWhileOnlyV2.detail: queued at version build-v1 but no live executor runs that version

notes: Hard rule 4 as written (version = build) strands an old build's in-flight work once the old container is gone: v2 executors will not dequeue v1 rows, even after resume.
Approval-enqueued work with no appVersion went to the latest version and ran fine — stranding only hits work that had already started.
Recovery requires keeping/starting an old-build executor until drained (or cross-version fork/rewind, which breaks the ID = idempotency-key rule).

t4d.title: Old code drains (SIGTERM, short window) while patched new code overlaps; new takes over and resumes the OLD branch
notes: Drain timed out with the workflow mid-step, so it stayed PENDING under the old executor; the new (patched) executor reaped it and DBOS.patch() returned false at the patch point, so the old step sequence resumed.
callProvider was replayed from its checkpoint: 2 provider attempts total for 2 actions, no re-call.

t5.title: Provider / connection failures → error classification and health state

attention.detail: connection_unavailable: required connection(s) not active: fake_provider:spike

notes: Non-retryable auth errors fail fast (1 call); retryable overload retries to the durableCalls limit; an expired required connection blocks before any model spend.

t6.title: ops.v_runs feeds health + attention without coupling them to DBOS internals
notes: Zero pg_depend edges from ops.* to dbos.*: DBOS migrations can never be blocked by our views.
Only ops.dbos_workflows() names a dbos table; agent_health/attention_queue read v_runs only.
v_runs status counts match the public DBOSClient.listWorkflows() API exactly.

t7.title: Supabase-style connection modes: direct / session pooler / transaction pooler (pgbouncer stand-in)

metrics.guardOn6543: refused: Refusing to start: aws-0-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com:6543 looks like a transac
metrics.listenProbeTxPooler: fail: LISTEN/NOTIFY probe timed out after 3000ms — not a session-capable connection

notes: Stand-in: local pgbouncer in session and transaction pool modes. Supabase's pooler is Supavisor; re-run t7 against the real project before locking.
DBOS 5.3 itself only WARNS behind a transaction pooler and falls back to polling; our startup guard turns that silent degradation into a refusal.

t8.title: Upgrade DBOS under live data (5.1.10 → 5.2.11 → 5.3.0)

transcript: migrations 122 -> 123 | recovery ok | v_runs: probe-pending-5.1.10=succeeded | agent_health rows=2 attention rows=0 | ops->dbos deps=0
migrations 123 -> 123 | recovery ok | v_runs: probe-pending-5.1.10=succeeded, probe-pending-5.2.11=succeeded | agent_health rows=2 attention rows=0 | ops->dbos deps=0

notes: Each hop: a workflow is SIGKILLed mid-flight under the old DBOS, then the new DBOS launches (running its migrations) and finishes it.
npm only carries the latest patch of each 5.x minor (5.0.2, 5.1.10, 5.2.11, 5.3.0), so this is two consecutive minor hops rather than a same-minor patch hop.
5.1.10 → 5.2.11 includes a real schema migration (122 → 123) applied with ops views in place; 5.2.11 → 5.3.0 has none.

t9.title: H1: zombie executor, heartbeat partitioned while the process keeps running

metrics.fenceLine: [recovery] FENCED: heartbeat not renewed for 3005ms (lease 3000ms); exiting before a peer takes over our work

notes: Partition = a test trigger that rejects only the zombie heartbeat write; its process, workflow and queue polling keep running.

Before the lease, the zombie kept running past its reap and dequeued the workflow its replacement had just resumed: two executions of one workflow in one process; the AI SDK durable-call guard failed the legitimate one, and our catch block recorded the run as failed. Now the zombie exits once it has been silent for 60% of DEAD_AFTER_MS, before any peer may reap it.

t9b.title: H1: zombie executor, process frozen past the reap, then wakes mid-way through the peer's run

metrics.fenceLine: [recovery] FENCED: heartbeat not renewed for 7052ms (lease 3000ms); exiting before a peer takes over our work

notes: The frozen process cannot dequeue, so the peer owns the resumed workflow. On waking, the zombie checks its lease before anything else and exits (code 70); any checkpoint it attempts first is rejected by DBOS (workflow no longer owned), and our catch blocks now rethrow that untouched instead of recording a failed run.

t9c.title: H1: same stall with the lease disabled: DBOS rejects the zombie's checkpoint and it stands down

metrics.fenceLine: [recovery] FENCED: this executor was reaped by t9c-b; exiting so work is not run twice

notes: Defence in depth: with no lease, the woken zombie finishes its in-flight model call and tries to checkpoint it. DBOS rejects it (DBOSWorkflowConflictError: no longer owned), our catch rethrows it untouched (no failed run recorded), DBOS parks that execution to adopt the owner's outcome, and the zombie's next heartbeat sees it was reaped and exits 70.
